selection_reason: Parameter validation -> changed from undefined to null check -> potential logic change affecting security
source_summary: The 'num' parameter comes from user code calling the get() method on jQuery objects. It can be any value including null, undefined, numbers, or other types.
sink_summary: When num is null/undefined: returns Array.prototype.slice.call(this) converting jQuery object to array. When num is a number: returns this[num] for array indexing.
guard_summary: The ternary check guards against null/undefined values. No explicit validation for numeric bounds or type safety. The change expands the guard from undefined-only to include null.
risk_pattern: Changed null/undefined check logic in array-like object accessor method. The change makes null and undefined equivalent for array conversion vs. element access decision.
enclosing_conditions: Conditional ternary operator checking num == null
context_summary: The get() method is used internally in manipulation and traversing operations to convert jQuery objects to arrays. The change affects whether null triggers array conversion (like undefined) instead of element access.
unresolved_facts: Exact security impact of treating null and undefined equivalently in this context
Whether any security-sensitive operations depend on the distinction between null and undefined in get() calls
